concepts.name: Physics studies the basic laws governing matter, energy, space and time
learning_points: Understand the relationship between physics and other sciences
Recognise the role of observation and experiment
Understand the importance of mathematical modelling
Identify major technological applications of physics

concepts.name: Physical interactions can be classified into fundamental forces
learning_points: Compare the broad characteristics and ranges of fundamental forces

concepts.name: Physics contributes to technology while technological developments create new opportunities for scientific investigation
learning_points: Understand interaction between science and technology
Recognise applications in energy and medicine
Understand the importance of responsible scientific development

concepts.name: Physical quantities are measurable properties expressed using numerical values and units
Different instruments provide measurements with different precision and least counts
Mass can be measured using appropriate physical and laboratory methods
Time is a fundamental physical quantity measured using clocks and periodic phenomena
learning_points: Recognise periodic phenomena used for timekeeping

concepts.name: Measurements contain uncertainties that must be quantified and reported appropriately
Significant figures communicate the precision supported by a measurement
learning_points: Apply significant-figure rules in addition and subtraction
Apply rules in multiplication and division

concepts.name: Dimensions express physical quantities in terms of fundamental quantities
Motion along a straight line can be described using position, displacement and time
learning_points: Use a reference point and coordinate axis

concepts.name: Speed and velocity describe how position changes with time
learning_points: Distinguish scalar speed from vector velocity

concepts.name: Acceleration measures the rate of change of velocity
Graphs provide a visual representation of one-dimensional motion
learning_points: Relate slope of position-time graph to velocity
Relate slope of velocity-time graph to acceleration
Interpret area under velocity-time graph as displacement

concepts.name: Kinematic equations connect displacement, velocity, acceleration and time for uniformly accelerated motion
learning_points: Derive the standard equations of uniformly accelerated motion

concepts.name: Motion can be described relative to another moving or stationary object
Vectors have both magnitude and direction
Vectors can be combined using geometrical and component methods
A vector can be resolved into mutually perpendicular components
learning_points: Use component methods in physical problems

concepts.name: Projectile motion combines horizontal uniform motion with vertical accelerated motion
An object can move with constant speed while its velocity continuously changes direction
An object maintains its state of motion unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force
Momentum is the product of mass and velocity
learning_points: Relate force to rate of change of momentum

concepts.name: Net force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum
learning_points: Derive F = ma for constant mass

concepts.name: Forces between interacting bodies occur in equal and opposite pairs
learning_points: Distinguish third-law pairs from balanced forces
Apply the law to practical situations

concepts.name: Friction opposes relative motion or tendency of relative motion between surfaces
Net inward force is required to maintain circular motion
learning_points: Understand banking of roads at the required level

concepts.name: Work measures energy transfer associated with a force causing displacement
learning_points: Use W = F s cos θ
Understand work as a scalar quantity

concepts.name: Kinetic energy is the energy associated with motion
learning_points: Relate work to change in kinetic energy

concepts.name: Potential energy represents stored energy associated with configuration or position
learning_points: Calculate gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface

concepts.name: Energy is stored when an elastic object is deformed
Mechanical energy remains constant when only conservative forces perform work
Power measures the rate of energy transfer or work done
learning_points: Relate power to force and velocity

concepts.name: Collisions conserve total momentum in an isolated system while kinetic energy may or may not be conserved

chapters.title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

concepts.name: Centre of mass represents the weighted average position of a system
learning_points: Calculate centre of mass for two particles
Understand centre of mass of a system
Apply centre-of-mass ideas to simple bodies

concepts.name: The total momentum of a system is related to the motion of its centre of mass
learning_points: Relate total momentum to centre-of-mass velocity
Apply conservation of momentum to systems

concepts.name: Torque measures the turning effect of a force about an axis or point
Angular momentum is the rotational analogue of linear momentum
learning_points: Relate torque to rate of change of angular momentum
Apply angular-momentum conservation to simple systems

concepts.name: Moment of inertia measures resistance to angular acceleration
learning_points: Calculate moment of inertia for standard bodies at the required level

concepts.name: Rotational motion follows laws analogous to translational motion
learning_points: Analyse rolling motion at the required level

concepts.name: Every pair of masses attracts each other with a force depending on their masses and separation
Acceleration due to gravity depends on Earth's mass, radius and location
Gravitational potential describes work done per unit mass in bringing an object from infinity
learning_points: Calculate potential due to a point mass

concepts.name: Minimum speed required for an object to escape a gravitational field without further propulsion
learning_points: Relate escape speed to planetary mass and radius

concepts.name: Satellites remain in orbit because gravitational attraction provides required centripetal acceleration
Kepler's laws describe the motion of planets around the Sun
learning_points: Relate Kepler's laws to gravitation at the required level

concepts.name: Materials deform under applied forces and may return toward their original shape when forces are removed
Stress is internal restoring force per unit area
Strain measures relative deformation
Within the elastic limit, stress is proportional to strain
learning_points: Understand yield and fracture regions at the required level

concepts.name: Elastic moduli quantify resistance to different types of deformation
Pressure in a fluid acts normally to surfaces and changes with depth
Pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted throughout the fluid
A body immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of displaced fluid
For steady incompressible flow, mass conservation relates flow speed and cross-sectional area
For ideal steady flow, pressure, kinetic and potential energy per unit volume are related
learning_points: Relate pressure changes to flow speed

concepts.name: Viscosity measures resistance of a fluid to relative motion between its layers
Surface molecules experience cohesive forces producing surface tension
learning_points: Understand excess pressure in drops and bubbles at the required level

concepts.name: Temperature characterises thermal state and heat is energy transferred because of temperature difference
learning_points: Convert Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin at the required level

concepts.name: Matter generally expands when heated
Specific heat capacity measures heat required per unit mass for unit temperature rise
Energy can be absorbed or released during phase change without temperature change
learning_points: Calculate heat involved in phase change

concepts.name: Thermal energy transfers through conduction, convection and electromagnetic radiation
Under suitable conditions, cooling rate is related to the temperature difference between an object and surroundings
If two systems are separately in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other
learning_points: Relate zeroth law to temperature measurement

concepts.name: Heat and work are modes of transferring energy
learning_points: Calculate work in simple thermodynamic processes

concepts.name: Change in internal energy equals heat supplied minus work done by the system under the standard sign convention
learning_points: Apply the law to standard processes

concepts.name: Different thermodynamic paths impose different relationships among pressure, volume, temperature and energy
learning_points: Compare work and heat transfer in standard processes

concepts.name: The second law establishes directionality and limits the conversion of heat into work
learning_points: Understand qualitative statement of second law
Distinguish reversible and irreversible processes at the required level

concepts.name: Heat engines convert part of absorbed heat into work while refrigerators use work to transfer heat against a temperature gradient
Macroscopic gas behaviour can be explained through microscopic motion of particles
learning_points: State basic assumptions of kinetic theory

concepts.name: Gas pressure results from molecular collisions with container walls
learning_points: Use the kinetic-theory pressure relation at the required level

concepts.name: Temperature is related to average translational kinetic energy of gas molecules
learning_points: Relate temperature to molecular kinetic energy
Relate molecular speed to temperature and molar mass

concepts.name: Energy is distributed among available independent modes of motion under suitable classical conditions
learning_points: Understand equipartition theorem at the required level
Relate degrees of freedom to internal energy

concepts.name: Oscillation is repeated motion about a mean or equilibrium position
In simple harmonic motion, restoring acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium
Mechanical energy remains constant in ideal simple harmonic motion
learning_points: Analyse energy at mean and extreme positions

concepts.name: For small oscillations, the simple pendulum performs approximately simple harmonic motion
learning_points: Derive time-period relation at the required level
Identify dependence on length and gravitational acceleration

concepts.name: A wave transfers energy and information through oscillations without net transport of matter
learning_points: Identify wavelength, frequency, amplitude and period

concepts.name: Wave speed is related to frequency and wavelength
learning_points: Understand dependence of wave speed on medium

concepts.name: When waves overlap, their displacements combine according to the principle of superposition
Superposition of suitable waves travelling in opposite directions can produce fixed nodes and antinodes
learning_points: Analyse standing waves on strings and in air columns at the required level

concepts.name: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave with measurable frequency, intensity and speed
learning_points: Relate amplitude and intensity to loudness
Understand speed of sound in different media

concepts.name: Superposition of waves with slightly different frequencies produces periodic variation in amplitude
Observed frequency changes when source and observer have relative motion
learning_points: Predict increase or decrease in observed frequency
